lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

The fifteenth publish is in work and is not live yet. It carries chain 44: summer's lights in the shake and the mend of the controls' stall. Stated by the helper machine that drew them: the page's first pictures were drawn again on the main branch as it stood at Status 248, 62 files in one commit, and the check of the first pictures passed at the first try (40 stills and the table agree with the framing). Measured here: the branch's head equals the one reported, its one commit touches the first pictures and the table in the page and nothing else, and the compiler is clean on it. Seen in the first picture attached: the four seasons as the page opens at 1920 wide, each whole, nothing torn and nothing missing; the four at phone size were looked at as well. Stated by a fresh security reviewer on the same commit: nothing blocks and nothing to warn of, no secret in the repo or in the build, and no address outside the site's own requested while the page runs. Running now: the whole test run and the build here, and a check of the built page on a helper machine at nine addresses with real shakes. It goes live when these are read and the reviewer's file hashes are compared with my own build.

The stand in the middle of a first shake, item 285, decision 275. Its mender asked for time until 4:45 AM MT Saturday, because the floors ask for many walks through the page and a walk takes 4 to 5.5 minutes on its one machine. That minute was not taken. Three helper machines are lent to it for the walks, one floor is trimmed on the main branch's side to one walk for each start and level, 24 walks, and a pair is still compared on one machine only. Its three orders went out at 11:04 PM MT, the walks are about 200 machine minutes over the three machines, and its report is now set by it for 1:00 AM MT Saturday. Stated by its mender as measured so far: with the mend, no shader program is linked during the shake in 8 of 8 shakes at low quality on pages that begin in spring and in fall. Ruled with it: the critic for the change of season runs once, on chain 45, and the fifteenth publish goes now from chain 44.

Winter's frost at film frame 668, item 275. The proof at 3840 at the masters' quality is slower than I said in Status 248. Stated by the two helper machines, each after the standard calibration line read equal: frame 668 took 796 s before and 838 s with the mend at 80 samples, frame 667 about 12 minutes at 74 samples, frame 620 about 5 minutes at 46 samples. Three of the seven pairs are drawn and on origin, the other four are due near 11:40 PM MT, and the judge's reading follows. Seen in the second picture attached, the table beside the foot cut at full size from each frame, before above and with the mend below: at rest, frame 620, the two read alike; in the motion, frames 667 and 668, the pale edge that stands beside the foot before is a soft band with the mend. That is a first look at a reduced view and not the ruling: I look at all seven pairs at full size before the mend is taken.

The second form of the counter of broken pixels, decision 276. Its report moves from 11:45 PM MT to 12:20 AM MT Saturday, because every floor is drawn before and after on the merged head and every draw alone. Stated by its mender as measured so far: film frame 680 at 1920 wide at the masters' tier with 24 samples comes out equal to the byte with the counter and without it, which is the floor the dropped form failed; the counter's eight test cases give the counts it marks as met and every picture is the same bytes before and after, one case at 24 samples not drawn yet; the page's start is not slower (medians 10.747 s before and 10.590 s after). One number is over my bar: on a frame at rest the counter costs 1.05 percent of the frame's time (41.228 s before, 41.661 s after, five pairs), where the floor says not more than 1 percent. The bar is not moved. It measures the heavier frame 680 as well, builds no other form and pushes nothing, and I rule once on its whole report. What the counter costs on a real graphics card is unknown.

The render instructions for his own computer. Decision 274 is in the builder's branch. The short test's floors are 38, 40, 40 and 44 dB, worked out by the one rule from the measures, and a unit test works them out again. The step where Brandon opens the sheet of pairs now says word for word what differs and is expected (where the runs of water stand on spring's glass, the fine grain of the moss, of the lumps on the table and of the sparkles) and the four things that are not expected and stop the render: stripes or blocks in that grain, a flat or blank area, a missing thing, a colour cast. Stated by the builder as measured on a hosted Windows machine: a test that is made to fail on purpose hands back what is needed to judge it from afar, 14 files of 7.5 MB with the measures beside their floors, the renderer's own name and the sheet of pairs. That sheet is the fourth picture attached; the two FAILS on it are the purpose of that job, which asks for 99 dB. Stated by the builder: after the main branch was merged in, the three reference pictures were drawn again and came out the same bytes, and its whole test run reads 1229 passed and 8 skipped. A last whole run on the hosted machines began at 10:58 PM MT and takes about 70 minutes. Then come its last report, the merge, a cold read by a fresh critic and the one line for Claude Code. No final render is started in the cloud.

Summer's lights, the second commit, on the lights' width at 3840. It was pushed with its report at 11:02 PM MT and is not taken yet. Stated by its builder as measured: every picture at 1920 wide is the same bytes as with the first commit and the eight guard stills equal the list in force, so only the 3840 film changes; at film frame 1470 six of seven measured lights are 3.1 to 3.5 pixels wide, inside the floor of 3 to 3.6, and one reads 2.86, 0.14 under; no peak is dimmer than with the first commit; its whole test run reads 1087 passed and 8 skipped. Seen in the third picture attached, nine places of frame 1470 at full size and at four times: broad soft bars with the first commit above, slim lines with narrow ends with the second below. Named by its builder as below the bar: at the size of a phone's feed the lights read fainter and fewer, 21 percent fewer lit pixels in a 400 pixel picture; a colour fringe on the slim lights near the glass's wall; the row of beads and the slabs while the globe travels stay as they were. Three helper machines now draw twelve frames of it at 3840 at the masters' tier, the strip 1468 to 1472 among them, and I look at them at full size before I rule. Its builder goes on to the seeds' dots, item 277.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. The fifteenth publish, with the stall's mend and summer's lights live. Chain 45: the frost line after its proof, the fireflies' second commit, the seeds' dots, the mend for item 285 and the Direct3D mend last, as each passes, then a critic for the change of season and a sixteenth publish. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code, then a cold read by a fresh critic. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard and BUILD COMPLETE.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks whiter and coarser than approved and its base darker. Summer's pond at rest (item 279). Fall's storm paler than approved. Spring's glass after a shake pale on pale, with square corners at the lower ends of a few runs. Spring's fence and trails. The fireflies' slabs while the globe travels, a faint second line, their width and their brightness (item 276). The seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277). The sand of the petals' mend at 4K before the encode, one small petal's softer edge and the petals' fringe at film frames 681 and 682 (item 278). The frost line at film frame 668 until its proof (item 275). The stall at the menu's options at low quality on a software renderer. A stand in the middle of the first shake on a page that begins in spring, summer or fall, live now (item 285). The gate of the masters still blind to a single broken sample of a frame, and the counter that would mend it 0.05 over its cost floor on a frame at rest. One compiler caution on Windows at fall's leaf cards (item 282). The square pressed fill of one menu option (item 283). One level in 14 corner pixels of the menu on a starved machine (item 284). Winter's four small items. Fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272). The poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273). Not verified: a real graphics card, a phone, Safari, Firefox, sound heard by a person.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.
